question.text: In an isothermal expansion of one mole of an ideal gas against vacuum from 10 litre to 100 litre at <math><msup><mrow><mn>27</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> , the quantity of heat absorbed by the gas is

solution.text: The quality of heat absorbed by the gas, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math>, here W is the work done by the gas. For free expansion i.e., expansion against vacuum, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>; at constant temperature, the internal energy of an ideal gas is constant and so <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Thus <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
